plugins.description: Pull requests, CI, issues and releases for projects on GitHub, as your GitHub login.
plugins.label: GitHub

steps.description: Makes a Draft ticket from a GitHub issue (its title, text, author and link), linked to it. When a ticket already links the issue nothing is made and the step leaves by `exists`: an issue is never imported twice. Output: `ticketId`, `ticketKey`, `issue` (owner/name#12) and `url`.
steps.title: Import a GitHub issue

steps.description: Adds a comment to a GitHub issue: by repo and number, or a ticket's linked issue (`unlinked` when it has none). Its URL is `{{steps.<id>.url}}`.
steps.title: Comment on a GitHub issue

steps.description: Closes a GitHub issue (by repo and number, or a ticket's linked issue: `unlinked` when it has none) as `completed`, `not_planned` or `duplicate` (GitHub's Close as duplicate, of the issue `duplicateOf`). It adds `labels` (keeping the others) and `comment` first. An issue already closed counts as done: nothing is changed.
steps.title: Close a GitHub issue

steps.description: Finds the ticket linked to a GitHub pull request (`exists`), or makes one (`created`): an external Draft in `project` with the pull request's title, text, author and link, linked to it, so it is never made twice. Without `create`, a pull request with no ticket leaves by `none`. Output: `ticketId`, `ticketKey`, `pr` (owner/name#12), `stage` and `closed` (Done or Won't do).
steps.title: The pull request's ticket

steps.description: Sets a pull request PDT didn't open to merge, as Merge does for an attempt's: auto-merge (GitHub holds it until the base branch's required checks pass) or the merge queue, with the strategy the repository allows (`queued`), or merged at once when GitHub can (`merged`). With `headSha`, only while its head is that commit (the one approved): `refused` with `code` `head_moved` otherwise. It never pushes to the pull request's branch: one that is closed, a draft or in conflict with its base leaves by `refused` with `code` and `reason`, as does a merge GitHub refuses.
steps.title: Merge a GitHub pull request

steps.description: Submits a review of a pull request as PDT's GitHub login: `request_changes` (the default), `comment` or `approve`, with `body` (or `fallback` when it comes to nothing). Its URL is `{{steps.<id>.url}}`.
steps.title: Review a GitHub pull request

steps.description: Closes a pull request without merging it, adding `comment` first. One already closed or merged counts as done: nothing is changed.
steps.title: Close a GitHub pull request

steps.description: Starts a GitHub Actions workflow by hand (`workflow_dispatch`) on a branch (default `main`) with inputs, as PDT's GitHub login. The repository is the run's project's unless `repo` names one. GitHub doesn't say which run it started: read what it makes (a pull request, a release) with the other GitHub nodes.
steps.title: Run a GitHub Actions workflow

steps.description: Reads the newest GitHub Actions run of a workflow (by its name, `release`) on a branch (default `main`), however it was started (a schedule, by hand), and leaves by its state: `passed`, `failed` (with `failedJobs`), `running` (queued or running), `cancelled`, or `none` when there is no run.
steps.title: Read a workflow's latest run

steps.description: Reads a pull request by its head branch or its number and leaves by its state: `open`, `merged`, `closed`, or `none` when there is none. Output: `number`, `url`, `title`, `state`, `merged`, `headSha`. With `ci` (and `branch`, its head) it reads CI too: an open one whose check failed on its head, or that the merge queue removed for failed checks, leaves by `failed` with `failure` (`ci` or `queue`), `ciUrl` and `failedJobs`. Between waits it polls one (a dry run takes `dryRunPort`, else `open` for a branch, `merged` for a number).
steps.title: Read a GitHub pull request

steps.description: Reads the latest published release (drafts and pre-releases don't count; with `prereleases`, the newest one, pre-releases included), or the one tagged `tag`. `found` with `tag`, `name`, `url` and `publishedAt`; `none` when there is none, or with `newerThan` when the latest is still that one. Between waits it polls for a release to be published.
steps.title: Read a GitHub release

steps.description: Looks for a day's nightly release (a published `X.Y.Z-nightly.YYYYMMDD` pre-release, PDT-288). `published` when there is one; before `dueHour` UTC `early`; `unchanged` when main has nothing its newest nightly or stable release lacks. Otherwise the nightly is missing: one Inbox item says so (once per workflow and day, else `already`), with Start it (`start`) and Ignore (`ignore`), and it looks again every half hour: the item closes by itself once the nightly is published (`published`), or after about a day (`expired`).
steps.title: Watch for the day's nightly

steps.description: Puts one Inbox item about a failed GitHub Actions run (`runId`) in the Inbox: its workflow, title, branch, what started it, its version or tag when it has one, its failed jobs and a link, with Re-run failed jobs (`rerun`) and Dismiss (`dismiss`). It looks at the run again every 10 minutes: the item closes by itself when a later attempt passes (`passed`), and a later failed attempt replaces it. After `watchFor` (default 7 days) it stops looking and the item waits for you. `cancelled` when the run was cancelled before it was reported, `none` when there is no such run, `already` when its attempt is in the Inbox already.
steps.title: Report a failed workflow run

steps.description: Re-runs the failed jobs of a GitHub Actions run (`runId`; every job with `allJobs`) as PDT's GitHub login, which needs the Actions write permission (else it fails: take its `error` port). Output: `runId`, the `attempt` it re-ran and the run's `url`. `none` when there is no such run.
steps.title: Re-run a workflow run's failed jobs

steps.description: Opens an issue in a project's GitHub repository, as PDT's GitHub login: from a ticket (`{{trigger.ticketId}}`; its title and description unless given, and the ticket links the issue), or in `project`'s repository. Output: `repo`, `number`, `issue` (owner/name#12), `url` and `ticketKey`.
steps.title: Create a GitHub issue

tools.does: Open an issue on the project's forge
tools.name: issue_create

triggers.description: A new issue in a GitHub repository: the ones in `repos` (any repo PDT's GitHub login can read), else the projects' own. Checked every minute; the first look at a repository only records where it is.
triggers.title: GitHub issue opened

triggers.description: A pull request PDT didn't open (not a ticket's branch) on a project's GitHub repository: from a fork, a bot such as Dependabot, or a collaborator (`kind`). The first look at a repository only records the ones already open. Checked every minute on the projects' GitHub repositories; outsiders' and bots' unless `kinds` says otherwise. Its title and body are outside input.
triggers.title: Outside pull request opened

triggers.description: New commits on a pull request PDT didn't open (its head moved): `previousHead` is where it was. Checked every minute on the projects' GitHub repositories; outsiders' and bots' unless `kinds` says otherwise. Its title and body are outside input.
triggers.title: Outside pull request pushed

triggers.description: A pull request PDT didn't open was closed or merged (`merged`). Checked every minute on the projects' GitHub repositories; outsiders' and bots' unless `kinds` says otherwise. Its title and body are outside input.
triggers.title: Outside pull request closed

triggers.description: A failed run of one GitHub Actions workflow (`workflow`, its file or name) in `repo` (else the project's), however it was started: on a schedule, by hand, by a push. Optionally only on `branch` and for some `events`. Checked every `every` (default 30 minutes); each failed attempt starts one run, and the first look only records where the runs are.
triggers.title: GitHub workflow run failed
